Label Maker Named One of Region's Top Employers
By Wilma Ostrander, Staff Writer
FAIRBROOK (February 26) — Vickery Label Company, which designs and prints product labels for food and drink makers, has been named to this year's Fairbrook Top Employers list. The company will be honored at a ceremony next month.
The list is compiled yearly by the Fairbrook Employers Council. For this year's edition, a panel reviewed 140 businesses and chose 25 of them. Vickery, which opened 22 years ago and employs 310 people, was one of the smaller firms named. Judges scored each business in three areas: how much control staff have over their hours, how much the company invests in learning, and how well it supports new employees. Vickery scored well in all three.
Under a flexible-hours arrangement, employees may start work at any time between 7:00 and 10:00 A.M. provided they work a full day. Each employee also receives $900 a year for outside courses, which last year paid for classes ranging from bookkeeping to painting. Finally, each new hire at the main office is paired for six months with an experienced colleague from a different department.
Sunil Batra, who joined the customer service team last year, said the pairing helped him from the start. "My mentor works in design, so when a client asked about artwork, I knew whom to call," he said.
Company managers plan to extend the mentoring program next year to staff at Vickery's warehouse in Redfield.

Listener Survey Results and Programming Plans
Prepared by: Station Manager's Office
Date: February 3
In December, Tamarack Community Radio invited listeners to complete a short survey on its Web site and in its printed newsletter. Of the more than 1,200 who replied, most are happy with the current schedule but want more chances to take part.
The morning program received the highest ratings of any show, and listeners praised its mix of local news and music. Hugo Lindqvist was pleased by these comments. He has opened every weekday broadcast at 6 A.M. for six years, and he chooses each song he plays. The program will stay as it is.
Listeners also valued last summer's live coverage from the Tamarack fair, where the station set up a temporary studio. Teodora Pavlic, who arranged the coverage with the fair's organizers, plans to return this year.
Many respondents, however, wished they could put their own questions to on-air guests. In response, the station will add a weekly hour in which local professionals answer questions phoned in by listeners. The first eight episodes will be carried only by our online stream, and the hour will join the Sunday schedule if audience numbers are strong. Offering recordings of each episode for download is still under discussion.
For the complete survey answers, contact Simon Farrow, listener research coordinator, at extension 3208.
Marit Lund, Station Manager

Greenvale Environmental Council
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Old Materials, New Uses
TILBURY (August 5) — When volunteers at last spring's river cleanup sorted through the 300 bags of waste they had gathered, they found many items that could still be put to use. Their suggestion that such items deserve a second life has led the Greenvale Environmental Council to establish the Made Again Awards, which will honor residents whose creativity turns discarded materials into practical objects.
Entries will be judged in three categories: Home and Furniture, Garden and Outdoors, and Toys and Games. Every piece must be made mostly from old wood, cloth, bottles, or other items headed for the trash. So that the judges can give each entry the attention it deserves, entrants may choose no more than two categories and submit one piece in each. The awards are open to anyone living in the Tilbury area, although those under 16 need a parent's permission.
Pieces may be brought to the council's office on Prescott Road from August 18 until October 10, each with an entry form from the council's Web site. A panel of council staff and two local furniture makers will review the entries in the second half of October, and winners will be announced on October 29. Their pieces will be displayed at Tilbury Public Library for four weeks, after which the makers may collect them there.
The council hopes to make the awards a yearly tradition and encourages residents to begin setting aside old materials now. Questions may be directed to Rhoda Benitez, events coordinator, at
[email protected]
.

Shared Plates Community Cookbook
This winter, the Weldon Food Bank will publish a cookbook of favorite dishes from local kitchens, and all profits will help fill our shelves.
As a thank-you, every contributor whose recipe is chosen will be sent the finished book, and each chosen recipe will be printed beside a full-page photograph of the dish.
Each entry should describe:
the name of the dish and its origin
a complete list of ingredients
the time it takes to prepare
any common allergens, such as nuts or milk
Please e-mail entries to
[email protected]
by September 30. Our volunteer editor reads every entry and will contact each chosen contributor about the photograph.
The Shared Plates Team
----------------------
To:
[email protected]
From: Lucia Gorman
Date: September 23
Subject: Shared Plates entry
Dear Shared Plates Team,
I would like to offer my family's lentil soup for your cookbook.
The recipe came from my aunt Edith, who made it every Sunday when I was a child. She cooked it with bacon for a smoky taste. I get the same taste from smoked paprika, so vegetarian guests can enjoy it too. I now bring a large pot of it to our neighborhood's autumn street fair each year.
The complete list of ingredients is dried lentils, carrots, an onion, garlic, a can of chopped tomatoes, vegetable broth, olive oil, and smoked paprika. From chopping the vegetables to serving, the soup takes about fifty minutes.
Thank you for considering it.
Lucia Gorman
Weldon
----------------------
To: Lucia Gorman
From:
[email protected]
Date: September 29
Subject: Your lentil soup
Dear Ms. Gorman,
I am happy to tell you that your lentil soup has been chosen for Shared Plates.
The next step is its photograph, and how it is taken is your choice. One of our volunteer photographers can visit your home on a weekday evening while you cook. Alternatively, you may take a clear picture yourself and e-mail it to me by October 13, since the book goes to the printer later this fall.
Finally, please tell me how you would like your name printed beneath the recipe.
Best regards,
Janet Munro
Weldon Food Bank
555-0187

Inkwell Mail
Newsletters that bring customers back
Choose the plan that suits the size of your mailing list.
Lite
: Up to 500 contacts. Design and send newsletters using ready-made layouts.
Complete
: Up to 5,000 contacts. Everything in Lite, plus scheduled sending and more ways to follow your results.
Our customers include cafés, hair salons, bookstores and gift shops, and no technical skills are needed to get started. New customers may use the Lite plan free of charge for their first 60 days. To open an account, visit our Sign Up page.
Inkwell Mail | Simple newsletters for small businesses
----------------------
www.inkwellmail.com/reviews
Home | Plans | Reviews | Help
Customer Reviews
My free period on the Lite plan ends this weekend, and my newsletters have already brought many first-time shoppers into my gift shop, which I opened three years ago. I have also recommended the service to a friend who owns a bakery.
Before I decide whether to continue, I have two concerns. Customers who join my mailing list at the counter are added to a spreadsheet, and every week I must retype those addresses into my contact list because the service will not accept the file.
Also, I am busy serving customers most of the day, so I handle business matters on my phone. However, I can see how many people opened each newsletter only when I sign in on a computer.
Frances Yeoh | Owner, Yarrow Gifts | Lite plan member
----------------------
www.inkwellmail.com/reviews/replies
Home | Plans | Reviews | Help
Our Reply
Dear Ms. Yeoh,
Thank you for your review. Regarding newsletter results, our mobile app shows how many readers opened each issue. The app is included in the Complete plan at no extra cost, and you can change plans at any time.
As for your contact list, an update released yesterday now lets subscribers on both plans import contacts directly from a spreadsheet file.
Finally, our template gallery, which we expanded this spring, offers more than 100 designs, including several for announcing new products. It is open to subscribers on either plan.
Best regards,
Omar Rahimi
Customer Support Manager, Inkwell Mail
